children: Copper rose, after falling more than 9% last week on deepening worries about global demand related to the selloff in artificial intelligence stocks.
The metal climbed as much as 1% to $12,287 a ton on the London Metal Exchange, after tumbling to the lowest level since March last week.

Used in wiring, copper soared to a record near $15,000 a ton in September on booming demand from data centers. But prices have plunged this month following the Democratic Party’s sweep of the US midterm elections, which fueled expectations for more scrutiny on AI build-outs.

There’s also uncertainty around whether President Donald Trump will impose tariffs on refined metal. Expectations for import levies had drawn metal into the US and drained supplies elsewhere, buoying prices and contributing to a supply squeeze in China.

In copper in particular, warnings that a record-breaking rally in prices was looking shaky have been growing louder for months. Throughout November, Xu says she watched as big short positions began to build in the Chinese copper market, even as physical supplies of metal fell to critically low levels on SHFE.

But while much of the drama last week was centered around China, the turmoil in copper has its roots in the US. Trump’s threat of tariffs on copper created an arbitrage trade that drew a massive share of global copper stocks into the US over the past two years, leaving the rest of the world tight on supplies and creating a mounting shortage in top consumer China.

At the same time, large financial flows have moved into copper and other metals that are needed to underpin infrastructure for AI, with prominent investors including billionaire Stan Druckenmiller touting the bullish outlook.

title: Copper rises after falling more than 9% last week on AI worries
